themes.title: What should the business own?
themes.question: Software as a source of differentiation
themes.description: If more software becomes practical to build, which customer experience or operating capability is worth making distinctive? Start with the workflow, its data, and who will maintain it, not a target for lines of code.
themes.test: Name the advantage, its owner, the buy-or-build alternative, and the ongoing cost of keeping it useful.

themes.title: What would justify the investment?
themes.question: AI economics and adoption
themes.description: A model benchmark is not a business case. Connect task quality, human review, integration, failure costs, and the ability to stop an experiment before deciding whether a smaller model or a new workflow helps.
themes.test: Specify the baseline, total workflow cost, acceptance test, and a reason to stop before the pilot starts.

themes.title: What evidence reaches the decision-maker?
themes.question: Risk, governance, and accountability
themes.description: A persuasive report and a high evaluation score can conceal weak evidence. Make sources, uncertainty, decision rights, and escalation visible before an AI-assisted recommendation becomes an operating decision.
themes.test: Trace a material claim to its source and identify who can challenge, approve, or reverse the decision.

industry_questions.question: Which parts of analysis can be accelerated without losing the evidence trail or expert accountability?
Where would a distinctive planning or service workflow matter more than another generic interface?
Which decisions need human approval, an inspectable record, and a reliable way to challenge the model?
What happens when a recommendation meets incomplete data, physical constraints, or an operator's exception?

buyers.question: Which AI investment deserves to go further?
buyers.situation: You have a promising pilot, an unclear business case, or a workflow that needs to change. The next decision is what to fund, buy, build or stop. A particular focus is document-intensive service businesses, where review work, exceptions and integration shape the economics.

buyers.question: Where does the opportunity survive contact with operations?
buyers.situation: You need to distinguish a plausible AI story from a capability a business can use and maintain. Start with one company, one workflow and a material decision before considering a wider portfolio programme.

review.title: AI Value and Execution Review
review.promise: A focused review of one business decision, with a recommendation you can examine and a next step you can test.
review.fit: For a leadership team with a pending investment or operating decision, a named decision owner, and access to the people and evidence needed to examine it.
review.not_fit: Not a general AI introduction, an open-ended transformation programme, a compliance certification, or a promise to justify a preferred supplier.
inputs: The decision, its owner and timing, plus the current workflow and alternatives already considered.
A baseline for cost, quality or service, including human review, exceptions and failure costs where relevant.
Agreed access to stakeholders, relevant system constraints and a bounded evidence sample, subject to confidentiality and data-handling terms.

outputs.title: A decision memo
outputs.detail: A recommendation and comparison of buy, build, partner and no-change options, with the evidence supporting each.

outputs.title: An assumptions and risks record
outputs.detail: What remains uncertain, what the recommendation depends on, who owns the decision, and the operating dependencies that could change it.

outputs.title: An investment gate
outputs.detail: A bounded next test, its baseline and acceptance criteria, and the conditions for continuing, changing direction or stopping.

steps.title: Agree the question
steps.detail: Check fit and conflicts, then agree scope, fee, timetable, access and confidentiality in writing before work begins.

steps.title: Examine the evidence
steps.detail: Work through the workflow, economics, data, evaluation and operating constraints with the relevant people. Make missing evidence explicit.

steps.title: Make the decision usable
steps.detail: Discuss the findings with the decision owner, record the trade-offs and hand over the memo and next-test criteria. Delivery is a separate decision.

review.boundary: A review can recommend buying an established product, using another provider, or not building. It is not an implementation contract or a guarantee of financial, technical or regulatory outcomes. Engagements remain subject to fit, availability and existing responsibilities.

delivery.title: Advice first. Delivery by a separate decision.
delivery.relationship: I am a founding partner of N13 Ventures, which backs KlusAI. That is a relevant commercial relationship if a review could lead to delivery work.
delivery.boundary: KlusAI may be an option where its capabilities fit. Any proposal has a separate scope and agreement, and alternatives remain part of the decision. I will disclose relevant interests before supplier recommendations; where a conflict prevents an appropriate review, we should not proceed on that basis.
